column1: # OneVoice VI ASR bias list: garment / textile factory vocabulary (draft v1, 2026-11-09)
#   display   default text written into the transcript when rewrite=yes
#   spoken    how workers SAY it, in Vietnamese syllables, variants separated by " | ".
#             GIPFormer only emits Vietnamese syllables and single letters, so the
#             decoder is biased toward these, never toward the English spelling.
#             "spoken => display" overrides the display for that one variant.
#   en        expected English rendering: a glossary for checking MT output
#   rewrite   yes = replace the spoken form with the display before MT;
#             guard = keep these phrases as spoken even where a shorter rule
#             would rewrite them (no bias, no glossary);
#             no  = bias the decoder only and keep the words as spoken.
#             Use "no" for native Vietnamese words: rewriting "thun" to "chun"
#             would also turn "áo thun" into "áo chun".
#   Policy: a term in this list is never left to Marian. Every row is `keep` in
#   both directions; `translate` exists only as an escape hatch.
#   mt        keep      = translate this term with `en` (glossary): before Marian
#                         the term becomes a numeric placeholder, afterwards `en`
#   vi_mt     the same for English -> Vietnamese: keep = when an English speaker
#             says an `en` form ("line 5", "presser foot"), the Vietnamese
#             forms go after the first with " | " ("line 5 | line five"); the
#             first is the one VI->EN writes.
#             name = keep where the English is capitalised, for a brand that is
#             also an everyday word: "Brother" stays Brother, "my brother" is
#             not the term and Marian still says "anh trai".
#             Parakeet often writes brands in lower case, so a name row adds
#             context forms with their own Vietnamese:
#             "brother machine => máy Brother" (these match any case).
#             The glossary matches the display form for rewrite=yes rows (case-
#             sensitive when it has a capital, so "thành công" never matches
#             "Thành Công") and every spoken form for rewrite=no rows.
# Spoken variants for brands, sizes and loanwords are PROPOSALS. Confirm or
# replace them from real recordings. After every edit run:
# A variant that tokenizes to <unk>, a one-token variant, two displays for one
# spoken form or a non-idempotent rewrite fails the compile.
# Names that are also ordinary words (Thành Công = success, Phong Phú = rich,
# Phương Đông = the East, "may mười" = sew ten) are only matched after
# "công ty" / "may" so ordinary speech is never rewritten.
